trial_court: Principal Senior Civil Judge, Tenali (HMOP.no.33 of 2017)
case_name: D Jagadish Babu vs D Sujatha
facts_of_case: The husband filed a divorce petition under Section 13(1)(ia)&(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife filed an interim maintenance petition under Section 24 of the Act. The trial court granted interim maintenance at Rs.1,500/- per month from the date of filing till disposal.

legal_principles.principle: A wife who is getting maintenance under Section 125 of CrPC cannot again claim interim alimony under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Jharkhand High Court held that the wife who is getting a maintenance of Rs.5,000/- as per an interim order passed in MC under Section 125 of CrPC cannot again claim interim alimony under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
cited_cases: Sangeeta v. State of Jharkhand, (2018) AIR JHARKHAND 57
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to determine the wife's entitlement to maintenance

legal_principles.principle: The Court below ought to have taken into consideration the huge expenses incurred by the wife on various litigations while fixing the quantum of interim maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The Court below ought to have taken into consideration the huge expenses incurred by the wife on various litigations and ought to have fixed an adequate amount towards interim maintenance.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to ensure fairness in determining the wife's entitlement to maintenance

outcome.final_order: The revision petitions are disposed of with a direction to the trial court to reconsider the quantum of interim maintenance awarded to the wife.
